expectation: Membrane or cell-surface stain on fibroblasts, CAFs, pericytes and vascular smooth muscle. These cells are common in tumour stroma. They should form long spindle-shaped strands and fibrous bands that wrap tumour nests and line vessels, and the dense epithelial or immune nests should be left unstained.
observed: A: every core shows yellow fibrous strands and networks around dark, nucleus-dense nests. B: wavy spindle-cell bands run between unstained blue islands. C: yellow tracks sit between blue cell-dense regions. D: elongated spindle cells with outline-like stain.
why: The stain is confined to spindle-shaped stromal cells that form strands around unstained nucleus-dense nests, which is the expected fibroblast and pericyte pattern; it is neither haze nor every cell lit alike.
notes: PDGFRb marks a stromal network of wavy spindle-cell bands that wrap and separate nucleus-dense nests in every core, while the nests stay dark. This is the expected pattern for CAFs and pericytes.
